resources.string: Learn what data CV Free uses, why it is needed and how you can manage your resume information.

When you register, your name, email address, user identifier (UID) and profile creation date are stored in Firebase. Registration, sign-in and password recovery are handled through Firebase Authentication. This information identifies your account and displays your profile.

You choose what to include: contact details, work experience, education, skills, a professional summary and optional sections. Editable resumes are saved in the application storage on your device. If you enable autosave, changes are kept while you complete or edit your resume. Only include information about other people, such as references, with their permission.

When you import a PDF or scanned document, information is extracted to fill in your resume. When AI import is enabled and runs, the document text and draft details are sent to Google services through Firebase AI Logic and Gemini to organize the information. This processing takes place outside your device. Avoid including unnecessary sensitive information and review the result before saving.

If you rate CV Free, your selected stars, optional comment, account UID, server timestamp and a submission identifier are stored in Cloud Firestore. The latest rating and a feedback history are kept to understand your experience with the app. The UID also limits submissions to one every 24 hours. Avoid including sensitive information in your comment.

CV Free uses Google and Firebase services to authenticate users, store profiles and feedback, configure features and process AI imports. Firebase Analytics records screens visited, actions, selected options and operation results. Firebase Crashlytics records crashes and technical errors to improve stability. These services may process device information and installation identifiers. Usage events do not include your name, email, password or resume content. Handled errors are reported without their original messages. These services may process information outside your country under their own terms and privacy policies.

Exported PDFs are saved to the location you choose with Android. These files are separate from editable resumes in the app. Android backups and transfers depend on your device settings. Deleting a resume from My CVs does not delete its exported PDFs or copies you have shared.

You can edit your profile name in Settings and update or delete resumes in My CVs. You can also change autosave and notification preferences. Signing out does not delete your account, profile or feedback stored in Firebase. Clearing app data in Android removes local app data, but does not automatically delete information stored in Firebase or exported PDFs.
CV Free\nDeveloped by Paul Guillen Acuña
